pharm: Probiotic preparation of viable Bacillus clausii spores used to restore intestinal microbial balance in diarrhea and during/after antibiotic therapy.
quick: May take with or without food; can mix in liquids
Generally considered low risk; limited data - use if needed
summary: Bacillus clausii is an oral probiotic of spore-forming bacteria used to restore gut flora and as adjunctive treatment of acute diarrhea, antibiotic-associated diarrhea, and other dysbiosis-related GI disturbances. Spores are acid-resistant and survive gastric transit. It is widely used in India and Europe (EMA/SmPC, BNF) but is not FDA-approved as a drug; dosing follows manufacturer SmPC. Generally well tolerated; caution is advised in severely immunocompromised or critically ill patients due to rare bacteremia reports with probiotics.
indications: Treatment of acute diarrhea (including in children) as adjunct to rehydration
Prevention and treatment of antibiotic-associated diarrhea / disturbances of intestinal flora
Restoration of intestinal microbial balance during dysbiosis
Adjunct in chronic/recurrent gastrointestinal disorders associated with altered flora (per local labeling)

dosage.n: Per manufacturer SmPC; doses vary by product (e.g., 2 or 4 billion spore preparations)

dosage.t: 2-3 times daily, spaced from antibiotic dose
dosage.n: Continue during and a few days after the antibiotic course

admin: Shake the vial well; the suspension may be taken directly or mixed in water, milk, or other beverage
Spores are acid- and antibiotic-resistant (depending on strain) and survive gastric passage
Space dosing from concurrent antibiotics by about 1-2 hours where advised
Do not add to very hot liquids (may reduce viability)
Store as directed; protect from heat and moisture
moa: Orally administered Bacillus clausii spores germinate and transiently colonize the gut, competing with pathogenic organisms, producing antimicrobial substances, and helping restore the normal intestinal microbiota disrupted by infection or antibiotics; may also support local immune and mucosal function.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to Bacillus clausii or any component of the preparation

preg: Limited data; probiotics are generally considered low risk. Use during pregnancy if clearly needed and per clinician judgment.
lact: Limited data; generally considered low risk during breastfeeding.

moderate: Concurrent oral antibiotics may reduce viability of non-resistant strains - separate dosing and continue probiotic through the course
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; can be mixed into cool drinks.

serious: Probiotic-associated bacteremia/sepsis (very rare, primarily in immunocompromised or critically ill patients)

monitoring: Resolution of diarrhea and GI symptoms
In immunocompromised/critically ill patients, watch for signs of infection
counsel: Continue rehydration (ORS) during diarrhea - probiotics are adjunctive, not a replacement
Can be taken with or without food and mixed into a cool drink
If taking antibiotics, space the probiotic by an hour or two and continue it through and after the course
See a clinician if diarrhea is severe, bloody, or persists beyond a few days
Store as directed and check the expiry date
pk: Local gut effect over days of use
Not applicable (acts locally in the gut, not systemically absorbed)
Not applicable (spores transit the GI tract)
Transient gut colonization; cleared after stopping
Store per manufacturer instructions; keep away from heat and moisture
pearls: Not FDA-approved as a drug; authored from EMA/SmPC and BNF/manufacturer information (widely marketed in India and Europe, e.g., Enterogermina)
Spore-forming and resistant to gastric acid; some preparations are resistant to common antibiotics, allowing concurrent use
Adjunct to oral rehydration in acute diarrhea - rehydration remains the cornerstone of treatment
Rare reports of probiotic bacteremia mean caution in severely immunocompromised or critically ill patients with central lines
Dosing and spore counts differ by product - follow the specific package labeling
missed: If a dose is missed, take it when remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose; do not double up.
overdose: No specific toxicity from overdose is expected; excess may cause mild GI upset (bloating, flatulence). Manage supportively.
refs: EMA / SmPC and product information (Enterogermina/Bacillus clausii)
